root_cause.text: The `neigh_xmit()` function had an inconsistent error handling path where it failed to free the skb when no neighbour table was found (when `rcu_dereference(neigh_tables[index])` returned NULL), causing a memory leak in the early return case.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that when `!tbl` was true, the code jumped to `out_unlock` label which only performed `rcu_read_unlock()` and then returned without freeing the skb. The fix changes this to jump to `out_kfree_skb` instead (after unlocking RCU), ensuring the skb is freed in all error paths. The commit message explicitly states: "neigh_xmit always releases the skb, except when no neighbour table is found" and identifies that callers like MPLS relied on neigh_xmit to always take ownership of the skb, making this unhandled case a leak vulnerability.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix RCU lock imbalance by explicitly unlocking before early return when neighbor table lookup fails.
intent_record.what: Modified the null check for `tbl` to explicitly call `rcu_read_unlock()` before jumping to `out_kfree_skb` instead of jumping to `out_unlock`. The braces around the if-block were also added for style consistency.
intent_record.how: This change fixes an RCU lock imbalance bug. Previously, when `tbl` was null, the code jumped to `out_unlock` which would attempt to unlock an RCU read-side critical section that was never properly entered due to the early exit. Now it explicitly unlocks the RCU lock before jumping to `out_kfree_skb`, ensuring the lock is released at the correct point in the control flow and preventing potential RCU stall warnings or deadlocks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused goto label to simplify code structure and eliminate dead code.
intent_record.what: Removed the `out_unlock:` label that was located immediately before the `rcu_read_unlock();` call in the neigh_xmit function.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates an unused goto label. The label was not referenced by any goto statement in the code path shown, making it dead code. Removing it simplifies control flow without altering the actual execution sequence, as `rcu_read_unlock()` is still called in the same location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify control flow by removing unnecessary goto label and directly returning error code from error path.
intent_record.what: Removed the 'out:' label and replaced 'goto out;' with 'return err;' in the error path, eliminating an unnecessary jump target and consolidating the return statement.
intent_record.how: The function now directly returns the error code from the error handling path instead of jumping to a label that simply returns. This eliminates one level of indirection while maintaining identical control flow and return behavior.

While the root cause mentions skb memory leak and this fix focuses on RCU lock imbalance, both are part of the same incomplete error handling path that needs to be corrected.

The key changes are: (1) Moving `rcu_read_lock()` to BEFORE the `rcu_dereference(neigh_tables[index])` call (line 3159-3160), (2) Adding a new label `out_unlock:` (line 3177) that ensures `rcu_read_unlock()` is called even when `tbl` is NULL, and (3) Changing the early return from `goto out;` to `goto out_unlock;` (line 3161). This fix ensures that when `rcu_dereference(neigh_tables[index])` returns NULL, the code jumps to `out_unlock:` which properly releases the RCU read lock before returning.
